properties.name: Boxwork ridge
properties.science_objective: Compare smooth ridge-top bedrock with the more nodular bedrock at the ridge/hollow edge, to test the idea that the ridges formed by cementation by circulating fluids.
properties.why_it_matters: Boxwork ridges and hollows record how groundwater cemented Mount Sharp's rock. NASA says boxwork patterns show water was still present underground while the surface was drying.
properties.position_source: PDS PLACES localized_interp.csv v42.0, frame ROVER, sol 4650, site 118, drive 2304 (planetocentric_latitude, longitude; last ROVER row for the sol 4650 image). The same row is in localized_pos.csv, so it is a localized solution, not an interpolated one. This is where the rover was, not the surveyed position of the feature itself. Uncertainty 0.5 m is the PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A §4.4.1.2 expected accuracy of localized rover positions against the HiRISE base map; it does not include the offset between the rover and the imaged feature.

evidence.text: Blog sols 4649-4654: the team documents the transition from smoother bedrock atop a boxwork ridge to more nodular bedrock; the ridges may be the result of cementation by circulating fluids.
NASA, 23 Jun 2025: even in the midst of this drying, water was still present underground, as shown by the boxwork patterns.
Position accuracy: localized positions have an expected accuracy of 0.5m compared to the base map (PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A, §4.4.1.2).

properties.name: Boxwork vein network
properties.science_objective: Examine networks of thin, cross-cutting filled fractures (resistant veins) in boxwork bedrock with APXS, MAHLI and ChemCam, and image a side view of the boxwork structures.
properties.why_it_matters: Filled fractures are where groundwater left minerals behind. NASA reports calcium sulfate veins in the bedrock between ridges, which were rare higher on the mountain.
properties.position_source: PDS PLACES localized_interp.csv v42.0, frame ROVER, sol 4618, site 118, drive 198 (planetocentric_latitude, longitude; last ROVER row before the sol 4619 image; next row is sol 4621). The same row is in localized_pos.csv, so it is a localized solution, not an interpolated one. This is where the rover was, not the surveyed position of the feature itself. Uncertainty 0.5 m is the PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A §4.4.1.2 expected accuracy of localized rover positions against the HiRISE base map; it does not include the offset between the rover and the imaged feature.

evidence.text: Blog sols 4620-4621: APXS and MAHLI investigated resistant veins, or filled fractures, at Pular and Socompa; ChemCam analysed veins at El Carrizo and Huasco.
NASA, 23 Jun 2025: bedrock between the ridges also contains calcium sulfate veins, left behind as groundwater trickled through rock cracks.
Position accuracy: localized positions have an expected accuracy of 0.5m compared to the base map (PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A, §4.4.1.2).

properties.name: Monte Grande hollow
properties.science_objective: Drill the Valle de la Luna bedrock in the Monte Grande hollow so CheMin and SAM can measure its mineralogy and volatiles, for comparison with a drill on the adjacent ridge.
properties.why_it_matters: NASA says comparing the mineralogy, volatile content and organic chemistry of ridges and hollows should reveal how the boxworks formed. This is the hollow half of that pair.

Uncertainty 0.5 m is the PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A §4.4.1.2 expected accuracy of localized rover positions against the HiRISE base map; it does not include the offset between the rover and the imaged feature.
properties.ez_theme: Hollow drill site: mineralogy and volatiles

evidence.text: Blog sols 4695-4701: Curiosity drilled its 44th hole at Valle de la Luna in the Monte Grande hollow; SAM evolved-gas analysis releases volatiles including H2O, CO2 and SO2.
Blog sols 4675-4681: the team chose Monte Grande as the next drill site, where SAM and CheMin will interrogate the boxworks.
Position accuracy: localized positions have an expected accuracy of 0.5m compared to the base map (PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A, §4.4.1.2).

properties.name: Nevado Sajama ridge drill site
properties.science_objective: Drill the ridge-top Nevado Sajama bedrock, about 10 m from the hollow drill site, and run DAN to estimate the ridge's hydrogen (and by extrapolation water) content.
properties.why_it_matters: NASA's team requested one drill target in a hollow and one on an adjacent ridge, only about 2 m apart in elevation, to compare their mineralogy, volatiles and organic chemistry.

properties.ez_theme: Ridge drill site: paired with hollow

evidence.text: Blog sols 4716-4722: drilling finished on sol 4718 at Nevado Sajama on the ridge; MAHLI saw fine veins in both targets; DAN gathered hydrogen (by extrapolation, water) data for the ridge.
Blog sols 4709-4715: the boxwork group requested one drill in a hollow and one on an adjacent ridge; there is a mere 2-meter elevation difference between hollow floor and ridge top.

properties.name: Boxwork and sulfate unit contact
properties.science_objective: Brush, image and analyse bedrock across the southern contact between the boxwork terrain and the layered sulfate unit, and compare it with the sulfate unit north of the boxwork.
properties.why_it_matters: NASA says magnesium sulfates are salty minerals that form as water dries up. Team framing, assumed: a candidate hydrated-sulfate (ISRU water) stop; no NASA yield figure is cited. The sol 4848 image shows sulfate terrain past the contact, not the contact itself.

properties.ez_theme: Sulfate unit contact: ISRU water candidate (assumed)

evidence.text: Blog sols 4845-4851: the drive took the rover just over the southernmost contact of the boxwork terrain with the surrounding layered sulfate unit; APXS and MAHLI analysed sulfate bedrock across it.
NASA, 23 Jun 2025: the rover is in a layer rich in magnesium sulfates, salty minerals that form as water dries up.
Position accuracy: localized positions have an expected accuracy of 0.5m compared to the base map (PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A, §4.4.1.2).
